pitchei_teshuva.en: That its impression remains. See Ba'er Heitev. See also Ginat Veradim, who writes that it appears to him that the Tur also agrees to this, namely that we require the writing to stand and endure. When the Tur writes that “its impression is recognizable,” he means that both requirements are necessary: it must endure and it must be recognizable. However, if it endures but is not recognizable, such as gallnut water on gallnut-treated parchment, as written below in se'if 3, or if it is recognizable but does not endure, such as fruit juice and the like, it is not valid. This is also written by the Pri Chadash, cited in Yeshuot Yaakov, se'if katan 1. He further writes that there is a type of thick, shiny ink called “papil bruneido,” known in our language as “glanz tint.” Its nature is that after the writing dries nicely, after a day or two, because of the thickness of the ink, the letters fall off and spring away from the paper. It appears that this is considered something that does not endure, and one must be careful not to write a get with this ink. See there. See also Get Mekushar, in Kuntrus Acharon, letter 6, who disagrees with him. He writes that it seems to him that this ink also does not spring off unless caused by something external, such as moving the paper and the like. Since it does not pass away on its own, it is properly called enduring. This is especially so because even after it springs off, an impression remains, and for a get an impression is sufficient. See there. The Torat Gittin here also disagrees with the Ginat Veradim on this matter. See there.

ezer_mikodesh.he: (עוד מצאתי) בסופר המציא תקנה להנגועות שבהגט פטירין. על ידי מה שבודק כל מלה ומלה תיכף לכתיבתה ואז עושה מב' ג' אותיות אות אחת גדולה כי כן צויתי לו פעם אחת כי אין קפידא לעשות קצת אותיות גדולים בהגט פטורין. גם שבסתוה"ק אין לעשות אתוון רברבין חוץ מהמקובלים כידוע על כל זה פשיטא דלא שייך כן בגט פטורין. ששם הכל בכתב מיד ה' השכיל בפרד"ס בכל אות ונקודה ותג וקוץ תלי תלים של הלכות עד אין סוף וכן היא בכל שנוי המקובל בכתיבת תנ"ך הק'. מה שאין כן בג"פ שהאותיות הגדולים שבו טעמם ידוע מדברי חז"ל מצד ידיעת פשטות המכוון ואין להקפיד יותר בזה. וגם במגילה ששמעתי מקפיד על האתוון רברבין שנוהגים עכשיו לכתוב מלבד המקובלים והרמז בהם מצד ר"ת או ס"ת אותיות שמות הק'. אך מכל מקום יש זכות בזה. שכמו דקיימא לן דלא שייך כל המוסיף גורע בתוספות תיבות בנוסח התפילות הק' וכמ"ש במק"א בזה. מההיא דסי' רס"ג באו"ח גבי הדלקת נרות דשבת"ק. שעל ידי תוספות אין גרעון להכוונה של זכרון זכור ושמור. וכן הוא בהרא"ש ז"ל סוף ר"ה לגבי ברכות שבתפילה. וכן הוא בזה שבודאי רמזי חכמה יש בשנוי האותיות שבמגילה גם כן כיון דקיימא לן שנכתבה ברוח הקודש. ות' רבתי דותכתוב כו' יש בה טעמים רבים על פי פרד"ס. אך על כל זה אין על ידי זה שום גרעון למכוון שבזה. מצד שכותבים גם אותיות גדולות שם שלא על פי הקבלה. כיון שאין הפסד בתוספות. וכיון שאין קפידא במגילה בדיעבד אם השמיט בה הסופר תיבות. לזאת מהראוי להיות מעלין בקודש לכבוד שמות הק' שהם בבחינ' הסתתרות בהמגילה הק' כידוע ועל כל זה הם השורש דכל המגילה הק'. והרשות נתונה בכל דור ליתן רמז הזכרה של שמות הק' המרומזים שם. ואין קפידא בתוספות אתוון רברבין בזה. ובגט פטורין פשיטא שאין גמגום או פתחון פה על זה בשום אופן. אך אתמול אירע שעשה א' דאנתתי גדולה. והיתה סמוכה לתיבת דהוית שלפניה. ולא הי' כשיעור י' לפי אותה הכתב ועל ידי שפוע ו' של על הא' ומה שצויתי להגביה גג הת' דדהוית בשפוע לימין הי' נשאר קרוב לכשיעור י' לפי כתב רוב הגט ורק חסר כל דהו באולי ובסדר הגט כתב שבחסר קצת אין קפידא כשאין שנוי משמעות אך הי' מקום לומר שנשער כפי גדלות הא' ולא לפי ערך הכתב של ת' שבצדה. ונראה שיש להכריע שהשיעור הוא כפי סגנון כתב דהת' שבצדה האויר דשם. כיון שהוא סגנון רובא דרובא דכתב כל הגט והאתוון רברבין הם בטלים במעוטם לגמרי והיו כלא היו ונהי דאי אירע בין שני אתוון רברבין כנ"ל. נראה להחמיר ולשער כפי האתוון רברבין כיון שאנו דנין על האויר שבין שני האותיות גדולות אין לנו לילך אחר רוב הכתב דהשטר. אך בהנ"ל כיון שהת' שבצדה היא ככל אותיות השטר. יש לדון על פיה. אך העיקר בזה לפי קריאת תנוק דלא חכים ולא טפש כבסדר הגט והראיתי לילד כבן עשר שנים וגם שמבין גם בכתב רש"י היטב. מכל מקום כיון שלא ידע פי' המלות והסתרתי לפניו חצי תיבות דהוית. ומכל מקום אמר שנראה שהא' שייכת לתיבה שלאחריה אך יש מקום לגמגם מצד שהתנוקות מורגלים בלימוד שיר הק' אקדמות מלין כו' שהוא נדפס באתוון רברבין בכל ראש שטה. וכן במחזורים בכל הפיוטים הם מורגלים באתוון רברבין בתחלה ולא באמצע ומה שלומדים לפעמים מחומשים מוגהים. שנדפס בהם אתוון רברבין שבתורה הק' באמצע המלות זהו מעוטא דמעוטא נגד כל אתוון רברבין שבמחזורים. ומכל מקום יש צד להכריע על פי מה שהנ' של אנתתי קרובה הרבה יותר להא' של אנתתי מצד הקירוב של הת' דהוית להא'. ועל פי זה ממילא יש בהיכר שהא' שייכת למטה. גם השנוי משמעות איננו כל כך משנה הענין ומצד שהי' הגט פטורין בשביל אפרושי מאיסורא. ששימשתו נדה וכמ"ש לעיל בזה הי' צד להקל. והי' הכרעה מהסבה הפשוטה מהשמים שהי' עיכובי' עד שנתאחרו החתימות סמוך לצאת הכוכבים וגם שרציתי להשמיט השאלות שבסדר הגט קודם הנתינה אחר החתימות. שיהיו אחר הנתינה. כיון שאין תקלה בזה. ואפשר שיהי' זה בלילה לגמרי בלי שום צד קפידא. אך על כל זה הי' סמוך כל כך עד שנוטה שהי' צאת הכוכבים גם אחר הדיבורים ההכרחיים קודם הנתינה ועל ידי זה סדרנו גט אחר היום ובעזהי"ת הי' בכשרות בלי פקפוק כלל. וגם שהחקירו' מהסופר והעדים שבסדר הגט בין החתימות לנתינה. אפשר לסדרם אחר הנתינה בלילה ממש בלי שום חשש גם בלי שום שעת דחק או הפסד מרובה רק כדי לחוס על איבוד הזמן והטרחא על כל זה סדר ביטול המודעת דהבעל שנית יש לו שרש בהפוסקים ז"ל. ויש להקדימו להנתינה בכל דאפשר. רצה הסופר לכתיב פ' כפופה בתיבת וואלף. ונזכר ונשאר רק נקודה והי' תחלה כה' ואחר כך משך פ' פשוטה ולא דיבק את הנקודה אל היו"ד שבתוך הפ' רק גררה. נראה שאין חשש בזה לכ"ע. שגם שכשגרר אות שלם. או גרר קצת מהאות כדי שיוכר על ידי זה יש בזה חששות. מכל מקום בזה שלא גרר מקצת מהאות. ולא אות שלם אין חשש. וגם שהי' מקום לומר pitchei_teshuva.en: So as not to come to engraving. See the Levush below, se'if 22, who writes: I am astonished by this reason, for we explicitly conclude in the second chapter of Gittin, as I wrote above in se'if 4, that engraving can be considered writing. Therefore, it does not appear to me that the reason for those who are careful not to write with these quills is the reason they gave. Rather, it appears that the reason is because the verse says “and he shall write,” which implies one act of writing, and not writing on top of writing. Here, if he writes with one of these quills, the quill engraves and digs the writing into the parchment, which by itself is valid, as we wrote above in se'if 4. Afterwards, the ink in the quill comes and fills the engraved writing made by the quill, and this becomes writing on top of parchment in a way that we hold is invalid, as above in se'if 10 regarding the care not to rule lines with lead. End quote. See Ginat Veradim, end of se'if katan 15, who explains the words of the Rama, “so as not to come to engraving,” to mean that perhaps the paper will be thin and the point of the quill will engrave the paper and puncture the letter with a hole going through it. He then cites the above words of the Levush and writes about them: I do not know from where he derived that writing on top of writing is invalid. According to his words, if one letter was written and there was not enough ink in it, and he passed the quill over it a second time, it would become invalid because of writing on top of writing. We have neither heard nor seen such a thing. On the contrary, we see what Maran writes below in siman 135, se'if 5. Even according to the one who says there that it is not a get, that is because it was originally written not for her sake, and the second writing does not help at all. However, if both writings were for her sake, everyone agrees that it is valid, and there is no invalidation because “the Torah said one writing and not writing on top of writing.” We have not heard such an exposition. Regarding the proof that the Levush brought from se'if 10, see Ginat Veradim below, se'if katan 45. Moreover, Terumat HaDeshen, siman 48, cited in Orach Chaim, siman 32, se'if 27, writes regarding letters and words that were partly erased, and the Levush himself copied this in Orach Chaim there. These are his words. See there. See Yeshuot Yaakov, se'if katan 2, who was asked about this matter, namely the practice of scribes to pass the quill over the get a second time before the signatures. The rabbi who asked wrote that this is improper, since the lower writing is not visible, and the upper writing is considered writing on top of writing according to the Levush. He answered him that there is no concern in this at all. He also mentioned the words of Mahari in Terumat HaDeshen, cited in Orach Chaim, siman 32, se'if 27, which oppose the words of the Levush. He writes that it appears proper to rule that the essential law follows Mahari, for we say that writing on top of writing does not help only where the first writing was written invalidly. He discusses this at length. See there. See Torat Gittin, se'if katan 3, who explains the words of the Rama differently. His explanation is somewhat similar to the reason of the Levush, but in another form: there is concern that he may engrave with the iron because there is no ink in the quill, and this too is considered engraved writing. Afterwards, he passes ink over the engraved place, and it is then like ink over red pigment, regarding which we say in Gittin 19 that one is liable twice, once for erasing and once for writing. Since he erased the first writing and wrote a second writing, we say that the witnesses have already fulfilled their agency. Certainly, if the scribe first wrote with red pigment and afterwards passed a quill with ink over it, the get is void, since the witnesses already fulfilled their agency with the first writing. So too here. These are his words. In my humble opinion, although he has said a wise idea, there remains a difficulty. The Rama should not have needed to warn about this here, for it is explained above, siman 122, se'if 1, that the husband gives permission to write from one get up to one hundred, until one is valid, with no concern. Even though the custom is to be stringent in every matter, nevertheless, since this is not the strict law, it is not appropriate to decree one safeguard upon another. Furthermore, it appears that once the custom is that the husband gives the parchment and ink to the scribe and says to him, “Here is the parchment and ink, write a get,” as explained in Seder HaGet, se'if 15, we see that the husband is particular that it be written specifically with ink. It is therefore not relevant to say that through engraving he fulfilled his agency. Although engraving is also considered writing, that is only where the husband did not instruct him to write with ink. But according to the custom, where he gives him the ink, he certainly has no permission to change. Even if he wrote with red pigment, it would also be nothing, and if so it is not relevant to say that he already fulfilled his agency. This requires further study. See Taz, se'if katan 3, who writes that it appears that if one needs to write with an iron quill, there is no need to be stringent at all.

בפיסול לבד. ובאם היה ד' במקום ר' אין די בגרירות תג הדלת משום דהוי ח"ת ואפילו בגרירות רגל או הגג לבד אינו די וצריך לגרור שניהם ותימא לי הרי איתא סוף פ' הבונה תנא הגיה אות אחת חייב אמר ר"ש כגן שנטלו לתגו של חי"ת ועשאו ב' זיינין רבא אמר כגון שנטלו לתגו של דלית ועשאו ר' ופירש"י רבא אמר כו' דלא הוי אלא הגהות אות אחת ובדבר מועט הוא הואיל וזהו תיקן הספר והוה ליה ככתב אות אחת כו' והנה המרד' הקשה מהי' ר"ש דמוכח מני דח"ת הוי כתב לענין שבת ומחלק בין חיוב שבת דמלאכת מחשבת אוסרה תורה וא"י מה יענה לתי' רבא דחשוב למחיקה דתג של ד' תקון ספר ואלו חשוב ח"ת לענין כתיבה מה התקון והאמת בח"ר שם כ' מהא דאמרינן הב"ע כגון שנטלו לגגו של חית שמעינן דכה"ג לא מקרי ח"ת שאינו אלא כמפריד בין ב' אותיות דבוקות וכן שנטלו לגגו של דלית ועשאו ר' אינו אלא כדיו שנפל על גבי האות ומעבירו עכ"ל נראה ברור דעיקר ראייתו מדרבא שאינו דומה לח"ת וא"כ צ"ע דעת יתר כל הפוסקים המדמים ענינים אלו לח"ת ואף בנפל טפת דיו שלוקח הרשב"א למושכל ראשון דלא נקרא ח"ת ולא מצינן דס"ל דר"ש פליג על רבא וס"ל דזה מקרי ח"ת וחיוב שבת שני ופוסקים כר"ש (א) They have the custom to be stringent, etc. The reason is that the letter does not look proper when the letters touch one another. But by strict law, touching letters in a Get are valid, even though in a Torah scroll it is invalid, because regarding a Torah scroll the verse says, you shall write them, meaning complete writing; and we do not derive the law of a Get from a Torah scroll, just as we do not derive parchment and ink requirements from a Torah scroll. So wrote Semag and the Rosh in Gittin chapter 2. A practical difference follows: if one wrote a letter and it is not surrounded by blank parchment below, according to all opinions it is valid, for the letter then appears proper. However, the Rosh did not give this reason, but wrote only that the custom is to be stringent that it be surrounded by blank parchment. One may say the reason is that initially we make it like a Torah scroll; according to this, even below it must be surrounded by blank parchment. See Responsa Mishnat Binyamin, siman 23, which I cited at the end of seif 7. The Maggid Mishneh wrote in chapter 4 that only when a child can read it is it valid according to those who validate; but when a child cannot read it, all agree it is invalid. According to those who are stringent, even if a child can read it, it is invalid. So too it appears from Semag and from Responsa Rivash, siman 56, and so Responsa Maharam of Lublin, siman 101, ruled. At first glance this does not appear so from the Rosh and the Tur, since they wrote that if ink fell into a letter and it is no longer recognizable, he may not remove the ink; this implies that if letters touch one another, even if it is not recognizable, he may repair it.

האות ע"י כתיבה פסול דבעינן שיהא כל האות ע"י כתיבה ושוב הביא בשם ר"מ אלשקאר סי' ה' אם נפלה טפת דיו והיא עשוי' כמין חצי אות לא אשכחן מאן דשרי להשלים האות ע"י כתיבה. אולם מלשון המג"א שם משמע שהוא ז"ל מסכים לדעת הב"י והרמ"א כאן ע"ש. גם בס' ג"פ סו"סק ל"י כתב וז"ל ולענין הלכה כיון דהכלבו וריב"ש ומרן ז"ל מסכימים דיכול להוסיף על האות כו' וכן מטיפת דיו להוסיף עלי' לעשותה י' או הכי נקטינן עכ"ל. אך זה ל"ע דמל' הג"פ כאן משמע דאף לכתחילה רשאי לעשות כן ואילו מדבריו ס"ק ל"ט לא משמע כן דשם האריך מאד בדברי הרד"ך הנ"ל (והזכיר שם דשורש דברי הרד"ך הוא בדין מ' פתוחה שנסתמה אי צריך למחוק כולה או סגי שימחוק קצתה עד שיפסיד צורתה ואחר כך ישלימה וע' בזה בב"י א"ח סי' ל"ב) ובסוף דבריו כתב וז"ל ולענין הלכה. הנה ראינו מערכה מול מערכה ומרן הב"י ז"ל דעתו מכרעת דמ"ם שנסתמ' בגרירת החרטום סגי בודאי דכן ראוי לפסוק בדיעבד אך לכתחלה ראוי לחוש לסברת הרד"ך והר"ם אלשקאר דס"ל דצריך לגרור כולה עכ"ל ולפ"ז ה"ה וכ"ש בדין דנפל טפת דיו להשלים האות ע"י כתיבה לאו שפיר דמי לכתחלה וא"כ יהיו דבריו סותרין זא"ז צ"ל דמ"ש בסוף ס"ק ל"ח דלכתחלה ראוי לחוש הוא רק על דרך מהיות טוב אבל לעיקר הדין נראה דעתו בכל הס"ק ההוא שמסכים לדעת מהר"י בן חביב ובנו הרלב"ח ומרן הב"י דאף לכתחילה די בגרירת החרטום לבד וכמו שפסקו כל האחרונים ז"ל בא"ח סי' ל"ב סעי' י"ח: שוב ראיתי בט"ז סק"י חולק על הב"י בדין דנפל טפת דיו וכתב דלא נראה לסמוך להקל לענין מעשה כי בודאי כל גוף האות צריך שיהי' ע"י כתיבה ומה מועיל מעט התוס' שע"י כתב אם לא היכא שהטיפה שנפלה היא עדיין לחה ומזיז בה ומושכה לכאן ולכאן ע"י (קולמס יבש או אפי' ע"י) סכין ועושה מזה אות שלם כגון ו' או י' בזה ליכא קפידא וכשר דזה הוה כאילו כותב הכל ע"י דיו מחדש וזהו פי' דברי הכלבו שהביא הב"י ע"ש. ומדבריו אלה נראה לכאורה דחולק ג"כ על דינו של התה"ד ורמ"א כאן אך מדבריו שבסק"ד מבואר דעל זה אינו חולק. גם בס' בית מאיר לקמן ס"ח מחלק בזה ודעתו בנפלה טפת דיו דחשיב ח"ת ממש העיקר כהפר"ח שחולק על הב"י וס"ל דאותו המיעוט כמאן דליתא אבל בנידון התה"ד (והרמ"א כאן) בהי' לו לכתוב כף כפופה וכתב נון כפופה ונמשכה רצועה מקצה אל קצה וצריך אחר גרירה למשוך ולעשותה כף בזה נ"ל אחרי שכל שנעשה על ידי כתיבה בפיסול ועכ"פ לא ממילא אינו אלא חק תוכות דרבנן ודאי י"ל דכל שהחקיקה לבד אינה גומרת צורת האות וצריך להוסיף עד שיעשה הצורה כראוי כ"ע מודים דשוב אף מדרבנן אינו נראה כחק תוכות ע"ש: ועיין עוד בג"פ ס"ק ל"ד שכ' וז"ל ומיהו מספקא לי לדעת הר"ם אנשקאר הנ"ל אם נפלה ט"ד והאריך בה ועשאה י' או נו"ן ויש בחלק שהאריך שיעור האות מהו דאפשר דלא פסיל בחצי אות חק תוכות אלא היכא דבתלקח יריכות בציר לה שיעורא ואותה טיפה שנפלה כבר משלמת לאות אבל היכא דהאריך באות טפי הו"ל אותה טיפה שנפלה כמאן דליתא ושרי לכ"ע והכי מסתברא עכ"ל. ועמ"ש עוד בזה בביאורי לסדר מהר"ם בסג"ר אות פ"ז:
pitchei_teshuva.en: When the entire letter was made in this manner. See Ba'er Heitev, who writes that since he is not performing an action, but where he does perform an action, and so on. See Taz, se'if katan 4, who writes that according to this, in the case below in se'if 9 of an open mem that became closed, if he closed the mem before completing it, he may scrape away the closure, since he still needs to add the slanted strip shaped like a yud. Therefore, he should first scrape away the attachment and then complete the letter. End quote. What Ba'er Heitev writes, “and if a little ink fell,” is the language of Beit Shmuel, se'if katan 5. It is obvious that this applies specifically in such a case, where the ink fell first and he then completed the letter through writing, in which case it is valid because the letter was completed validly. But if the drop itself completed the letter, it is certainly invalid, for everything follows the completion. This is also explicitly clear from the words of the Beit Yosef. See there, and see what I wrote on this in my commentary to Seder Gittin, in Seder Get Rishon, letter 87. What Ba'er Heitev writes, “The Beit Shmuel wrote that if an invalid person wrote the letter,” and the Pri Chadash writes that it should simply be invalidated, from this wording it sounds as though the words of the Pri Chadash refer only to the ruling of the Beit Shmuel, namely where an invalid person wrote the letter and a valid person completed it. In truth, however, this is not so, as I saw in Beit Meir, who cites him. The Pri Chadash also disagrees with the main ruling of the Beit Yosef in the case where a little ink fell, and with the ruling of Terumat HaDeshen and the Rama here, where part of the letter was made through chok tochot and still needs correction. See there. See Magen Avraham, Orach Chaim, siman 32, se'if katan 23, where it is also clear that this law is not agreed upon. There he cites the Radach, that even if one completely erased the drop and completed the letter by writing, it is invalid, because the entire letter must be made through writing. He then cites Rabbi Moshe Alashkar, siman 5, that if a drop of ink fell and formed something like half a letter, we do not find anyone who permits completing the letter through writing. However, from the wording of the Magen Avraham there it appears that he agrees with the opinion of the Beit Yosef and Rama here. See there. The Ginat Veradim, end of se'if katan 30, also writes: As to the halacha, since the Kol Bo, Rivash, and Maran agree that one may add to the letter, and similarly may add to a drop of ink to make it into a yud or a vav, this is how we rule. End quote. However, this requires analysis, because from the language of the Ginat Veradim here it sounds that one may do so even ab initio, whereas from his words in se'if katan 39 it does not sound so. There he greatly elaborates on the above words of the Radach, and he mentions there that the root of the Radach’s words concerns the case of an open mem that became closed, whether one must erase all of it or whether it is enough to erase part of it until its form is ruined and then complete it. See Beit Yosef, Orach Chaim, siman 32, on this. At the end of his words he writes: As to the halacha, we have seen one side against the other, and Maran the Beit Yosef’s view is decisive, that where a mem became closed, scraping away the protrusion is certainly enough, and this is the proper ruling after the fact. However, ab initio one should be concerned for the view of the Radach and Rabbi Moshe Alashkar, who hold that one must scrape away the whole thing. End quote. According to this, the same, and all the more so, applies in the case of a drop of ink that fell and one wishes to complete the letter by writing: this is not proper ab initio. If so, his words contradict each other. One must say that what he wrote at the end of se'if katan 38, that ab initio it is proper to be concerned, was only as a matter of extra care. But as to the essential law, throughout that se'if katan his view appears to agree with Mahari ben Chaviv, his son the Ralbach, and Maran the Beit Yosef, that even ab initio it is sufficient to scrape away only the protrusion, as all the later authorities ruled in Orach Chaim, siman 32, se'if 18. I later saw that Taz, se'if katan 10, disagrees with the Beit Yosef regarding the case of a drop of ink falling. He writes that it does not appear proper to rely on this leniently in practice, because the entire body of the letter must certainly be formed through writing. What does the small addition made by writing help? This is only where the drop that fell is still moist, and one moves it and pulls it here and there with a dry quill, or even with a knife, and from it makes an entire letter, such as a vav or a yud. In such a case there is no concern, and it is valid, for it is as if he wrote the whole thing anew with ink. This is the explanation of the words of the Kol Bo cited by the Beit Yosef. See there. From these words it appears at first glance that he also disagrees with the ruling of Terumat HaDeshen and the Rama here, but from his words in se'if katan 4 it is clear that he does not disagree about that. The Beit Meir below, se'if 8, also distinguishes between these cases. In his view, where a drop of ink fell, which is considered actual chok tochot, the main ruling follows the Pri Chadash, who disagrees with the Beit Yosef and holds that the small added part is considered as if it does not exist. But in the case of Terumat HaDeshen, and the Rama here, where one needed to write a bent kaf and wrote a bent nun, and a strip extended from end to end, and after scraping one still needs to draw and make it into a kaf, in that case it appears to him that since everything was made through writing, albeit invalidly, and at least not automatically, it is only rabbinic chok tochot. Certainly one can say that wherever the scraping alone does not complete the form of the letter, and one must add until the form is made properly, everyone agrees that it no longer appears to be chok tochot, even rabbinically. See there. See further Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 34, who writes: However, I am uncertain according to the above-mentioned opinion of Rabbi Moshe Alashkar, where a drop of ink fell and one extended it and made it into a yud or a nun, and in the part that he extended there is enough measure for the letter. What is the law? Perhaps half a letter made through chok tochot is invalid only where, if the legs were removed, the necessary measure would be lacking, and the drop that fell already completes the letter. But where he extended the letter beyond that, the drop that fell is considered as if it does not exist, and it is permitted according to all. This seems reasonable. End quote. See also what I wrote about this in my commentary to Seder Maharam, in Seder Get Rishon, letter 87.

pitchei_teshuva.he: מוקפות גויל. עבה"ט ועיין בתשו' מהר"ם לובלין סי' ק"א אודות הגט שניתן כבר ונמצא בו דבקות אותיות ד' בה' מתיבת דהוית ופסק מאחר דרוב הפוסקים מכשירים אחר הנתינה א"צ להחמיר לחוש לסברת הא"ז וראבי"ה שהובא בסדר גט דהר"י מינץ סי' פ"ח דמבואר שם דפסול גם אחר הנתינה כי הם מיעוטא דמיעוטא נגד רוב הפוסקים כו' אך בתנאי דתינוק דל"ח ול"ט קורא אותו פשיטא שיש להצריך גט אחר ופסול הוא כו' ע"ש ועיין בג"פ ס"ק כ"א שתמה עליו דהא תיבת דהוית היא מן הטופס ואפילו דילג תיבה זו לגמרי לא שינה משמעות הגירושין ולא איכפת לן בדיעבד אחר נתינה כמ"ש בסי' קכ"ו סעיף מ"ט (ושם בסעיף ל"ה בהגה) כ"ש דאין לפוסלו אחר נתינה משום דיבוק אע"ג דתינוק אינו יכול לקרותה ע"ש: ועיין בתשו' נ"ב סי' פ"ה על דבר הגט שהובא ממקום רחוק ע"י שליחות ומחמת שנפל למים נטשטשו כמה אותיות והדיו נתפשט רשומו חוץ להאותיות בין האותיות ובחלק שבין שטה לשטה באופן שגם חוץ להאותיות הקלף שחור אלא שעכ"פ האותיות ניכרים כי גוף האות שחור מאד ומה שחוץ להאות הוא דיהה הרבה אם לפסול גט כזה מחמת קלקול האותיות ומחמת אינו מוקף גויל. וכתב הא ודאי דכתב ע"ג כתב אפי' כתב שני משחיר טפי לא מהני אבל אני מסופק אם נפל דיו על קלף חלק ונשא' הקלף שחור ואח"כ כתב במקום הזה בדיו המשחיר יותר באופן שהאותיות ניכרים היטב אם זה מקרי כתב או לא ונראה שדבר זה שנוי במחלוקת בין רש"י ור"ת בגיטין דף י"ט ע"א דרש"י פי' בד"ה הא דעפיצן שהרי מראה הקלפים כמראה הכתב ואינו ניכר (גם בש"ע לעיל סעי' ג' כתב כלשון הזה) משמע דאם היה ניכר שפיר מיחשב כתב אבל ר"ת שם בתוס' ד"ה דיותא כתב דדיו אין עושים מעפצים דהיכא כתבינן ס"ת ע"ג קלף שהוא מעופץ ע"ש והא ודאי שדיו שעשוי ממי עפצים (עם קנקנתום) . ניכר הוא על הקלף מעופץ ואפ"ה לא מהני לר"ת. וכיון דבדין זה לא קיי"ל כר"ת כמבואר בטור יו"ד סי' רע"א ובב"י שם מוכח דאם משחיר יותר וניכר על הקלף מחשב כתב. ועוד נראה שזה מבואר בש"ע סי' קכ"ה ס"ח בהגה שכ' רמ"א ויש מחמירין אפי' אם האות ניכר כו' (עמ"ש שם) וכיון שלפי דברי השואל יש כאן בנ"ד עיגון גדול שהבעל במדינה רחוקה ואין שיירות מצויות ורעש מלחמה לכן שפיר פסק הרב השואל להכשיר הגט ואין חשש מחמת היקף גויל ולא משום קלקול האותיות ובלבד לעיין היטב שיהיה עכ"פ כל התורף כל אות בבואה שלו קיימת עכ"ד ע"ש. ועיין בתשו' נו"ב תניינא סי' קי"ג בדבר הגט שבתיבת היום נמשך כעין קו דק ומחבר ראש הוי"ו למ"ס סתומה ואמנם ניכר שאינו מן הדיו רק מפסולת הנייר כתב לא ידעתי בזה שום חשש כיון שהקו הזה אינו דיו רק מן הנייר בעצמו ולמיחש שמא לא מועיל כתב עליו ששחור בלא"ה ולהיות כדיו ע"ג דיו ע' בחבורי נו"ב סי' פ"ה ותראה שאין זה חשש עכ"ד.
pitchei_teshuva.en: Surrounded by parchment. See Ba'er Heitev. See also the responsum of Maharam Lublin, siman 101, concerning a get that had already been given and was found to contain attached letters, namely a dalet attached to a heh in the word דהוית. He ruled that since most decisors validate it after delivery, there is no need to be stringent and be concerned for the view of the Or Zarua and Ra'avyah, cited in Seder Get of Rabbi Yehuda Mintz, siman 88, where it is explained that it is invalid even after delivery. They are a very small minority against the majority of decisors. However, this is on condition that a child who is neither especially wise nor foolish can read it. If not, it is obvious that another get must be required and it is invalid. See there. See Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 21, who questions this, for the word דהוית is part of the standard formula. Even if this word were omitted entirely, it would not change the meaning of the divorce and we would not be concerned after the fact once the get was given, as written in siman 126, se'if 49, and there in se'if 35 in the gloss. All the more so, it should not be invalidated after delivery because of attachment, even if a child cannot read it. See there. See the responsum of Noda BiYehuda, siman 85, concerning a get that was brought from a distant place by an agent. Because it had fallen into water, several letters became blurred, and the impression of the ink spread outside the letters, between the letters and in the spaces between lines, so that even outside the letters the parchment was black. Nevertheless, the letters themselves were recognizable, because the body of each letter was very black, while what was outside the letter was much lighter. The question was whether such a get should be invalidated because the letters were damaged and because they were not surrounded by parchment. He writes that certainly writing on top of writing does not help, even if the second writing is blacker. However, he was uncertain in a case where ink fell on blank parchment and the parchment remained black, and afterwards one wrote in that place with ink that blackens more strongly, so that the letters are clearly recognizable, whether this is called writing or not. It appears that this matter depends on a dispute between Rashi and Rabbenu Tam in Gittin 19a. Rashi explains, under the words “where it was treated with gallnuts,” that the appearance of the parchments is like the appearance of the writing, and the writing is not recognizable. The Shulchan Aruch above, se'if 3, also uses this language. This implies that if it were recognizable, it would properly be considered writing. But Rabbenu Tam there in Tosafot, under the words “ink,” writes that ink is not made from gallnuts, for how could we write a Torah scroll on parchment that was treated with gallnuts? See there. Now certainly ink made from gallnut water with vitriol is recognizable on gallnut-treated parchment, and nevertheless according to Rabbenu Tam it does not help. Since in this law we do not rule like Rabbenu Tam, as is explained in Tur, Yoreh Deah, siman 271, and in the Beit Yosef there, it is proven that if it blackens more strongly and is recognizable on the parchment, it is considered writing. Furthermore, it appears that this is clear from Shulchan Aruch, siman 125, se'if 8, in the gloss, where the Rama writes, “There are those who are stringent even if the letter is recognizable,” as I wrote there. Since, according to the questioner, there is great concern of igun in this case, because the husband is in a distant country, caravans are not common, and there is the upheaval of war, the rabbi who asked ruled properly to validate the get. There is no concern because of being surrounded by parchment, nor because of damage to the letters, provided that one examines carefully that at least throughout the essential text of the get, every letter remains in its proper outline. These are his words. See there. See also Noda BiYehuda Tinyana, siman 113, concerning a get where, in the word היום, something like a thin line extended and connected the head of the vav to the closed mem. However, it was recognizable that it was not from the ink, but only from waste in the paper. He wrote: I do not know of any concern in this, since this line is not ink but only from the paper itself. As for the concern that perhaps writing over it does not help because it is black anyway, and it would be like ink on top of ink, see my work Noda BiYehuda, siman 85, and you will see that this is not a concern. These are his words.

pitchei_teshuva.he: אותיות דבוקות. כתב בס' ג"פ ס"ק כ"ד וז"ל בענין דיבוק האל"ף והפ"א וצדי"ן ושיני"ן שנדבקו היודין שלהם לאותיות עצמן במקום אחר מלבד מקום דיבוקן נשאל דלב"ח סי' א' לענין ס"ת והשיב דהר"ר מנחם כתב דוקא כשנדבקה באות אחרת אבל אם דבוקה בעצמה כל שלא נפסדה צורת האות כשרה וכ"נ מדברי הרמב"ם והוא ז"ל מסיק דצריך תיקון גם כתב שם כי יש קצת דבוקים אפי' שיהיו באות עצמה משנים קצת צורת האות כגון נדבק רגל הקוף וכן ראש אמצעי של השין למעלה או י' הפ"א למטה וה"ה ראשי העי"ן או הצד"י הרי נשאר חלק שבפנים סתים מכל צדדיו צריכין תיקון ולא בגרירה לבד אלא שיגרור קצת מהאות באופן שלא ישאר שמה עליה ויכתבנה אח"כ כי היכא דלא להוי חק תוכות כו' עכ"ל ועמ"ש לקמן ס"ח ס"ק י"ג:
pitchei_teshuva.en: Attached letters. Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 24, writes as follows: Regarding the attachment of the alef, peh, tzadi, and shin, where their yuds became attached to the letters themselves in another place besides their proper point of attachment, the Bach was asked about this in siman 1 concerning a Torah scroll. He answered that Rabbi Menachem wrote that this applies specifically where it became attached to another letter. But if it is attached to itself, as long as the form of the letter was not ruined, it is valid. This also appears from the words of the Rambam. He himself concludes that it requires correction. He also writes there that there are some attachments, even within the letter itself, that slightly change the form of the letter. Examples include the leg of a kuf becoming attached, the middle head of a shin becoming attached above, the yud of a peh becoming attached below, and the same applies to the heads of an ayin or tzadi. In those cases, the inner space is left closed on all sides. These require correction, and not by scraping alone. Rather, one must scrape away part of the letter in such a way that its name no longer remains upon it, and then write it again, so that it not be chok tochot. End quote. See what I wrote below, se'if 8, se'if katan 13.

pitchei_teshuva.he: דאין להפריד. עבה"ט ועיין בשו"ת הגאון החסיד מהר"ש זלמן זצ"ל מלאדי שכ' דנ"ל שגם רמ"א בהגה לא מיירי אלא כשיש שעת הדחק לכתוב גט אחר אם לא בהוצאה מרובה כגון שהסופר והעדים נחוצים לדרכם ומהעיכוב יגיע להם הפ"מ וכה"ג שא"א לכתוב אחר אלא בדוחק והפ"מ אזי יש לתקן כו' שכ"ה משמעות הלשון שע"י הדחק טכ"פ אפשר לכתוב גט אחר. אבל כשא"א כלל לכתוב גט אחר היינו מקום עיגון שהתיר רמ"א בהדיא בד"מ וכ"כ הלבוש. ואתי שפיר דל"ק קושיית הב"ש מסעי' ט"ז בהגה וע"ז סמך רמ"א ולא הוצרך להזכיר זה בס"ו עכ"ד ע"ש עוד וע' בס"ק שאח"ז:
pitchei_teshuva.en: That one should not separate them. See Ba'er Heitev. See the responsa of the holy gaon Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, of blessed memory, who writes that it appears to him that even the Rama in his gloss speaks only where writing another get would be a pressing circumstance, unless one incurred great expense. For example, the scribe and witnesses are hurrying on their way, and the delay would cause them great financial loss, or a similar case where another get cannot be written except with difficulty and great loss. In such a case, it may be corrected. This is the implication of the language, that through difficulty another get could at least be written. However, where it is completely impossible to write another get, that is a case of igun, which the Rama explicitly permitted in Darkei Moshe, and the Levush writes similarly. This works out well, and the question of the Beit Shmuel from se'if 16 in the gloss is not difficult. The Rama relied on this and therefore did not need to mention it in se'if 6. These are his words. See further there, and see the following se'if katan.

pitchei_teshuva.he: בשעת הדחק לתקן. עח"מ וב"ש שתמהו בדברי כרב בהגה והובא קצת בבה"ט סק"ז והסכימו לדינא דבשעת הדחק ועיגון או שכבר ניתן כשר אפי' בלא תיקון רק יותר טוב שיתקן ואפי' ע"י אחר מפני מראית עין וכשהבעל או הסופר שהוא שליח הבעל כאן אפי' בלא עיגון כשר לתקן כשעדיין לא חתמו העדים ע"ש ועיין בס' תו"ג שכ' דנראה לו שגם דעת הרמ"א ז"ל כן הוא רק שיש ט"ס בדבריו וחסר תיבת או וכצ"ל ויש מקילין בשעת הדחק או לתקן קודם שיחתמו כו' פי' דבשעת הדחק כשר אפי' בלא תיקן או אפילו שלא בשעת הדחק יכול לתקן קודם שיחתמו כו' (וע' בס"ק שלפ"ז) וכ' עוד דבמקום שיש פסול גמור כגון שיש יתור אות בתורף אינו מועיל לגרור האות ע"י אחר אפי' בשעת הדחק דכיון שהגט בכה"ג הוא פסול גמור א"כ לא עשה הסופר שליחותו כלל דהא מה"ט מותר הסופר לכתוב גט אחר כמבואר בסי' קכ"ב והוי כאלו כל הגט נכתב שלא בשליחות וכשמחקו אחר הוי ככתבו אחר שאינו שליח הבעל. אבל כשמגררו הסופר בעצמו אין בו פסול רק משום שיש גרר בגט והוי כנכתב ע"ד שיכול לזייף וכשר ע"י ע"מ במקום עיגון כגון בעוזב דת וכה"ג שאין שהות לכתוב אחר דאפי' בתפילין מהני גרירת האות להכשיר ואין לומר בזה דהוי כחק תוכות כיון דע"י גרירה לתקן התיבה דזה אינו דדוקא באות שייך לומר כן ולא בתיבות ע"ש וכ"כ בג"פ ס"ק ל"ו ע"ש:
pitchei_teshuva.en: In pressing circumstances, to correct it. See Chelkat Mechokek and Beit Shmuel, who question the words of the Rav in the gloss. Part of this is cited in Ba'er Heitev, se'if katan 7. They agree as to the law that in pressing circumstances and a case of igun, or if the get has already been given, it is valid even without correction, although it is better to correct it, even by another person, because of appearances. When the husband, or the scribe who is the husband’s agent, is present, then even without igun it is valid to correct it before the witnesses have signed. See there. See Torat Gittin, who writes that it appears to him that this was also the opinion of the Rama, of blessed memory, but that there is a scribal error in his words and the word “or” is missing. The correct reading should be: “There are those who are lenient in pressing circumstances, or to correct it before they sign.” This means that in pressing circumstances it is valid even if it was not corrected, or that even not in pressing circumstances one may correct it before they sign. See the previous se'if katan. He further writes that where there is a complete invalidation, such as an extra letter in the essential text of the get, it does not help for another person to scrape away the letter, even in pressing circumstances. Since in such a case the get is completely invalid, the scribe did not fulfill his agency at all. For this reason, the scribe is permitted to write another get, as explained in siman 122. It is as if the whole get was written without agency, and when another person erases it, it is as if another person, who is not the husband’s agent, wrote it. But when the scribe himself scrapes it away, there is no invalidation except because there is an erasure in the get, and it is like a document written in a manner that could be forged. It is valid through witnesses of delivery in a case of igun, such as where the husband has abandoned the religion or the like, where there is no time to write another. Even with tefillin, scraping away a letter can help to validate it. One should not say in this case that it is chok tochot, since the word is corrected through scraping, because that concern applies specifically to a letter and not to words. See there. Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 36, also writes this. See there.

pitchei_teshuva.he: מוחי' ובידו. כתב הב"ש הטעם משום לעז גיטין הראשונים. ודוקא דבר שאינו אלא חומרא בעלמא חיישינן משום לעז וע' תה"ד סי' רל"ב ע"ב. ועיין בס' ג"פ ס"ק ל"א כמה חילוקים בענין זה דאין מוציאין לעז על הראשונים וע' עוד בתשו' מהרי"ט ח"א סי' פ"ו מ"ש בזה. ועיין בס' טיב גיטין בליקוטי שמות סק"ז (ויובא קצת לקמן סי' קכ"ט סי"ד ס"ק ל"ו) שב' דנראה פשוט דלא שייך הוצאת לעז על גיטין הראשונים כ"א בדבר שהוא נוהג בכל גיטין הניתנין שם כגון בשם העיר או בנוסח גופו של גט אבל בשמות האיש והאשה דכל גט הוא ענין בפ"ע כו' אין בזה משום מוציא לעז ע"ש. ועיין בתשו' הראנ"ח ח"ב סי' י"א שכ' דלא אמרו אתה מוציא לעז על דורות הראשונים אלא בדבר של אישות לפי דהבאים מזרעם אשר הם אתנו יהיו פגומים אבל בשאר איסורים לא אמרינן כן דמאי דהוה הוה ע"ש והבאתי דבריו אלו ג"כ בפ"ת ליו"ד סי' רי"ד סק"ד ושם העירותי ע"ז דבמג"א סי' ל"ב סוס"ק מ"ח לא משמע כן ע"ש. ועיין באה"ט לקמן סי' קכ"ח ס"ק י"ג:
pitchei_teshuva.en: They protest, and it is in his power. The Beit Shmuel writes that the reason is because of casting aspersions on earlier gittin. Only where the matter is merely a stringency do we worry about such aspersions. See Terumat HaDeshen, siman 232, amud 2. See Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 31, who gives several distinctions in this matter, namely when we do not cast aspersions on the earlier ones. See also the responsa of Maharit, part 1, siman 86, regarding what he writes on this. See Tiv Gittin, in Likkutei Shemot, se'if katan 7, which will be cited in part below, siman 129, se'if 14, se'if katan 36. He writes that it appears obvious that the concern of casting aspersions on earlier gittin applies only to something that is practiced in all gittin given in that place, such as the name of the city or the wording of the body of the get. But regarding the names of the man and the woman, where each get is a matter unto itself, this does not involve casting aspersions. See there. See the responsa of Raanach, part 2, siman 11, who writes that they said “you are casting aspersions on the earlier generations” only in matters of marriage, because those who descend from them and are with us would be rendered blemished. But with other prohibitions we do not say this, for what happened has happened. See there. I also brought these words in Pitchei Teshuva, Yoreh Deah, siman 214, se'if katan 4, and there I noted that from Magen Avraham, siman 32, end of se'if katan 48, this does not seem so. See there. See also Be'er Heitev below, siman 128, se'if katan 13.

להעבירו כשר אלא דבזה צ"ע למעשה אך בהעביר השעוה יש להכשיר בפשיטות ע"ש:
pitchei_teshuva.en: A drop of ink. See Ba'er Heitev, which is the language of the Beit Shmuel. Regarding what he wrote, that it sounds as though biblically it is void, see Beit Meir, who discusses this at length and concludes that the essential ruling appears to follow the Rashba and the implication of most decisors: anything made through writing, even if it was made invalidly, but at least not automatically, is only rabbinic chok tochot. See there. In the middle of se'if katan 38, Ginat Veradim also appears to hold this way, unlike the Radach, siman 1. He mentions there that Rabbi Yehuda ben Chaviv and his son, the Ralbach, in responsum siman 1, also appear to hold this way, namely that every such case is only rabbinic because of a resemblance to chok tochot. This is also implied by the words of Semag and Sefer HaTerumah in the laws of tefillin. See there. What he further wrote, “even if a drop of ink fell after the letter was completed,” means to exclude the view of the Kol Bo and Semak, cited in the Beit Yosef, who hold that if ink fell after the letter had been made properly, there is no concern. See there. See Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 31, who also writes that we follow the view of most decisors who disagree with the Semak. Nevertheless, he writes that if she was divorced with a get in which this occurred, we count her as possibly divorced. There is also a practical consequence in using the view of the Semak and those who agree with him as a supporting factor, such as where the letters themselves became attached to their yuds, for example alef, peh, tzadi, and shin, aside from their proper place of attachment. There is a dispute among the great authorities whether they need correction, as written above and cited in our words above, se'if 6, se'if katan 8. If this attachment occurred after the letter was written properly, and one merely scraped away the attachment, this becomes a double doubt. In a case of igun and pressing circumstances, one may rely on the view of the Semak and those who support him. This can also be learned from the words of the Ralbach, siman 1. There is also a practical consequence from the view of the Semak and those who support him in a case where letters became attached to one another. It was already explained in se'if 6 that according to the strict law, attachment of letters does not invalidate a get, except that the custom is to be stringent that the letters be surrounded by parchment. If so, when the attachment is below, one may be lenient in pressing circumstances. But if it is above, one may be lenient only after the fact in a case of great igun. These are his words. What he further wrote, “and there is no distinction between whether the letter is moist or dry,” means to exclude the view of the Levush, who writes that if the ink fell after the letter had dried, and one removed the ink, it is valid. See there. See also Beit Shmuel, who writes that Seder Maharam explains the words of the Levush as referring to a case where a drop of ink fell on the letter and did not spread at all. See what I wrote about this in my commentary to Seder Gittin, in Seder Get Rishon, letter 87. What he further wrote, “however, in a case of igun, even a complete error may be scraped away,” until “and so ruled the Taz,” see Taz, se'if katan 17. He writes there that according to the strict law it is valid to write over an erasure if one wishes to rely on witnesses of delivery and bring them before the court, except that this is not the practice because we do not differentiate. In a case of igun, one need not be concerned, especially according to our custom to take the get after it is given and tear it, so that the matter will never come to relying on the witnesses of signature. I saw this reasoning in Terumat HaDeshen regarding another matter. These are his words. See there. What he further wrote, “and in the signatures of the witnesses it is permitted even ab initio to erase the entire letter,” makes clear that it is specifically writing over an erasure that is permitted. But chok tochot is invalid even in the signatures of the witnesses. This is also stated explicitly in the Taz there, and so writes the responsum of Mahari Weil, siman 27. See there. See Beit Shmuel below, siman 130, se'if katan 20, where it is explained that if chok tochot occurred in the name of the father of the witnesses, it is valid in a case of difficulty and igun; and if it occurred in the word עד, “witness,” it is valid even without difficulty or igun. See there. In Ginat Veradim above, se'if katan 18, it is explained that his view is that in the name of the father of the witnesses one may also be lenient even without difficulty and igun. See there. What he further wrote, “and if they already signed,” see what I wrote about this in my commentary to Seder Get Rishon, letter 87. What Ba'er Heitev further wrote, “and if a drop of wax fell, he may scrape away the wax,” see Ginat Veradim above, end of siman 124, who inclines toward stringency even if the wax was removed, because perhaps it resembles chok tochot. See there. However, Get Mekushar, in Kuntrus Acharon, letter 9, disagrees with him. His opinion is that even if he did not remove the wax, as long as it is possible to remove it, the get is valid. In practice, this requires further study. But if the wax was removed, it should plainly be validated. See there.

beit_shmuel.he: שום טשטוש. הטעם משום חשש זיוף וכתב בד"מ יזהר שלא ירד שום זילוף או שום לכלוכית על הקלף משום כשכותבים עליו נראה כמחוק וכשיפלו גשמים על הכתב אין נותנים הגט דנעשה שחור והוי כדבר שיכול לזייף ולא יכתוב על המחק מטעם הנ"ל אף על גב ע"פ הדין מותר לכתוב ע"ג דבר שיכול לזייף כמה שכתב בסימן קכ"ד והיינו אם ע"מ לפנינו מכל מקום לכתחלה יש ליזהר כי שמא ימותו ע"מ וכן אם זבוב מושך מאות לא ימחוק ואל יהיה בין תיבה לתיבה ובין אות לאות שום דבר מחוק ודבר שיכול לזייף לכן אין כותבים ע"ג דבר גרד, וכבר כתבתי במקום עיגון כשר כתב בד"מ ניקב בצד האות ולא באות כשר:
beit_shmuel.en: Any smudge. The reason is concern for forgery. Darkei Moshe wrote that one should be careful that no drip or dirt fall on the parchment, because when one writes over it, it appears erased. If rain falls on the writing, the get should not be given, for it turns black and is like something that can be forged. One should not write over an erasure for the same reason. Although by strict law it is permitted to write on something that can be forged, as written in siman 124, namely where the delivery witnesses are before us, nevertheless ab initio one must be careful, lest the delivery witnesses die. Likewise, if a fly dragged ink from a letter, one should not erase it; there should be no erased matter between word and word or between letter and letter, because that is something that can be forged. Therefore one does not write over something scraped. I have already written that in a case of agunah it is valid. Darkei Moshe wrote that if it was punctured beside the letter and not in the letter, it is valid.

pitchei_teshuva.he: חק תוכות. עיין בס' ג"פ ס"ק י"ח שכ' דהא דפסלינן חק תוכות בגט דקדק מהריב"ל ח"ג סי' ס"ט מדברי הרשב"א ומהרי"ק שורש ע"א דהיינו דוקא בתורף אבל בטופס לא כו' וע' לקמן סי"ו בהגה ומ"ש שם. וכ' עוד בס"ק כ"ה דבסדר גט דהר"י מינץ סי' פ"ה כתב וחק תוכות דפסול לא מהני בי' העברת קולמס ע"ש ובס"ק ל"ג הביא דכ"כ בסה"ת סי' ר"ה ובהג"א פ"ב דגיטין (גם המג"א סי' ל"ב ס"ק כ"ו כתב כן) והוא ז"ל כ' על זה דמדברי התוס' פ"ב דגיטין דף י"ט בד"ה דיו ע"ג דיו משמע מדבריהם היכא שהכתב השני מתקן כלום חשיב כתב וא"כ יש לדון דהעברת קולמס ע"י חק תוכות משוי לי' חק יריכות וע' לקמן סי' קל"א ס"ה דהעברת קולמס לשוויי' לשמה אינו גט וי"א דחוששין לו וא"כ יראה דה"ה לענין העברת קולמס לשווי' חק יריכות דחוששין לו עכ"ד ועיין בס' בית מאיר שכ' אילו הייתי כדאי לחלוק מסברא הי' מסתבר לי דאפי' למ"ד דהעברת קולמס לשמה אינו מועיל מ"מ העברת קולמס על ח"ת מהני דזה הוה כאילו כותב על נייר חלק עש"ב:
pitchei_teshuva.en: Chok tochot. See Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 18, who writes that Mahari ben Lev, part 3, siman 69, inferred from the words of the Rashba and Maharik, shoresh 71, that the fact that we invalidate chok tochot in a get applies specifically to the essential text, but not to the standard formula. See below, siman 16 in the gloss, and what is written there. He further writes in se'if katan 25 that Seder Get of Rabbi Yehuda Mintz, siman 85, writes that where chok tochot is invalid, passing a quill over it does not help. See there. In se'if katan 33, he brings that Sefer HaTerumah, siman 205, and Hagahot Ashri, chapter 2 of Gittin, write likewise. Magen Avraham, siman 32, se'if katan 26, also writes this. He himself writes about this that from the words of Tosafot in the second chapter of Gittin, page 19, under the words “ink on top of ink,” it is implied that where the second writing corrects something, it is considered writing. If so, one can discuss whether passing a quill over chok tochot makes it into chok yerechot. See below, siman 131, se'if 5, where passing a quill over the writing in order to make it for her sake does not make it a get, and some say that we are concerned for it. If so, it appears that the same would apply to passing a quill over it in order to make it into chok yerechot, that we should be concerned for it. These are his words. See Beit Meir, who writes: If I were worthy to disagree by reasoning alone, it would seem logical to me that even according to the opinion that passing a quill over the writing to make it for her sake does not help, nevertheless passing a quill over chok tochot does help, because this is like writing on blank paper. See there at length.

יתקנן קודם שיכתוב כדת משה וישראל. הטעם כתב בט"ז שלא יהיה מחוסר מעשה אחר גמר הכתיבה קודם הנתינה ויכול לתקן אפילו אינו שעת הדחק כיון דליכא תיקון כ"כ ול"ד לפירוד אותיות לכן יכול לתקן כאן כל זמן שלא חתמו העדים אם צוה הבעל או יתקן הסופר כמ"ש בסמוך:

pitchei_teshuva.en: And there are those who are stringent. See Beit Shmuel, se'if katan 12, who writes that Seder Maharam, letter 87, is stringent in this matter if it is in the essential text of the get, even in a case of igun. But this does not seem to be the view of Maharik. See Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 37, who also writes that in a case of igun and pressing circumstances, even according to Maharik, one may erase the drop of ink. Even if the drop touches the sides of the letter, if a child reads it properly, he may scrape away the drop and it is not chok tochot. See there further, where he writes that if a drop of ink fell and the form of the letter did not change, and before the ink was absorbed into the parchment or paper the scribe quickly sucked the ink with his tongue and wiped it from the get, and it is not recognizable that there had been an erasure, it is logical to be lenient in this. Since even if the drop had dried there, it would not have changed the form of the letter, and according to the strict law it would be permitted to erase it even with a knife, except that as a stringency we do not erase with a knife because the erasure is noticeable, in this case one should not be stringent because the erasure is not noticeable. All the more so, if gallnut water or coffee water fell on the get and made stains, the get should not be invalidated, since the letter is recognizable. However, if actual ink fell on one word, or even on one letter, whether in the essential text or in the standard formula, and it changed the meaning of the divorce, and if the ink had dried there it would have ruined the form of the letter, but the scribe quickly wiped it with his tongue, it appears to me that it is invalid and is considered chok tochot. See there, and see what I wrote above, se'if katan 7. See the responsum of my revered grandfather, Panim Meirot, part 2, end of siman 47, concerning a get brought by an agent from far away. The woman’s name was שאשה, and there were two dots inside the heh of שאשה. It was recognizable that because the get had been folded, the leg of the alef in שאשה reached into the hollow of the heh, and because of the moisture of the ink, some ink from the leg of the alef attached itself inside the heh. It looked like two yuds inside the hollow of the heh. He wrote: In siman 125, se'if 8, it is explained that if a drop of ink fell inside the letter, and there are those who are stringent even if the letter is recognizable. The Bach explains that this applies not only where it is now read as another letter, such as where ink fell inside a bet and it became a peh, but even where it did not become another letter. However, it appears that there the case is where the form of the letter did not change, but nevertheless the drop is attached to the upper roof or to the leg on the side. This is unlike our case, where it is not attached, but merely an extra dot inside the heh. It is possible that everyone agrees that he may erase the extra part and that this is not chok tochot. It must be that the Chelkat Mechokek, se'if katan 12, also understood this way, for he asks that if the intent is to be stringent ab initio, there would have been no need to write it, as cited in Ba'er Heitev, se'if katan 10. If the view of these stringent authorities were that even if a drop of ink fell in the middle of the hollow of a letter, such as in a bet or heh, and it does not touch the sides, it is still prohibited, then what is his question from letters touching each other? There, they touch and meet; here, the drop does not touch any side. Rather, it is necessarily so that the view of the stringent authorities applies only where the drop touches the roof of the letter or the side, and nevertheless the form of the letter is recognizable. But if it does not touch any side, everyone agrees that it may be scraped away. All the more so in a case of igun, where one may rely on those who are lenient even if it touches the side of the letter but does not cover the letter entirely. If so, in our case it is obvious that one may rely on this in a case of igun. These are his words. See there. See above, se'if katan 14, and also the following se'if katan. See also what I wrote below, se'if 16, se'if katan.

pitchei_teshuva.en: The letter is recognizable. See Ba'er Heitev in the name of Chelkat Mechokek, who raised a difficulty. See the responsum of Noda BiYehuda, siman 85, who writes, after explaining there that if a drop of ink fell on blank parchment and one wrote over it with darker ink, it is called writing, as cited above, se'if 6, se'if katan 7. He writes as follows: To me, this is not difficult. There, some of the ink itself with which the letter was written touched another letter. If so, what does it help that the letter is recognizable? In any case, it is not surrounded by parchment, and ab initio we are stringent with a get as with tefillin and a Torah scroll. But here, a drop of ink fell, and since the letter is recognizable, the ink of the letter is certainly darker and therefore recognizable. What spread from the drop onto the surrounding parchment does not ruin it, because even the place of the drop is called parchment in relation to the blackness of the letter. If so, there is no basis to be stringent because it is not surrounded by parchment. The Rama therefore teaches us that nevertheless we are stringent ab initio. Even aside from this, I do not know why the Chelkat Mechokek was astonished. According to both answers that the Beit Yosef writes in Orach Chaim, siman 32, regarding why we validate a case of a hole, see there, here, where a drop of ink fell and does not reach another letter, and it happened after the letter had already been written, according to both answers there is no concern of surrounding parchment. The Rama therefore teaches us that nevertheless one should be stringent ab initio. These are his words. See there.

(א) Even in the place of its writing. Beit Yosef concluded so and emended the Tur's text from "its giving" to "its writing." Not only as a matter of halachah did he rule to be concerned even for the place of writing. My teacher and father-in-law, z"l, disagreed and said that one need not be concerned for the place of writing. Beit Yosef's words appear correct, for this is similar to what is written in siman 129 seif 7 regarding one who has another name in the place of writing.

(ג) Some say it is invalid. My teacher and father-in-law, z"l, wondered at this, for in chapter 3, folio 6, Rav Papa asks: what is the law if he stipulated that the paper between the lines should be his? The Gemara leaves it unresolved. Why not derive that the Torah said "one book," not two or three books? It answers: it is needed where the lines are joined. From here one might hear that the reason for joined lines is so that it be one book, or so that it not be possible to forge and write between the lines, as these reasons are found in Seder Gittin. Nevertheless, invalidity is not heard from there, and the language "it is needed where it is joined" implies that ordinary gittin are not joined, only that this case speaks so. In all other kingdoms they do not write joined lines at all; therefore even not in a case of agunah, if one erred and wrote lines that are not joined, another get is not needed, and this one may be given ab initio. In my humble view, one can defend the invalidating view from the sugya. The questioner was uncertain whether even the space between the lines must belong to the woman, and therefore whether that space must be whole, such that it is not enough that the empty part be cut away even if some remains at each edge. The Gemara asks that it should obviously be invalid, for the Torah requires one book, meaning that even the space between the lines should be whole; only then is it one book. It answers that the verse was not needed for the space between the lines, but for the writing of the get, that the lines should be joined into each other. The empty parchment between the lines is not what the verse discusses, and that remains unresolved. Thus the verse indicates the joining of the writing, and this is required. This also answers the difficulty from siman 130, where if he left part of the get and wrote it on a second page, writing two pages is valid; we consider the second column as though placed below the first, like the laws of open and closed sections in tefillin. Therefore Rama ruled well that one should be lenient only in a case of agunah.

However, in Orach Chaim, siman 32, se'if 18, this language is not used. There it says: “An open mem whose opening became attached and it became closed,” and so on. pitchei_teshuva.en: To rule lines for it. See the new responsa of Bach, siman 87, who writes that regarding the case where the scribe wrote one line in the get somewhat far from the ruling line and it bent slightly downward, we have not found any concern in this. See there. See Pitchei Teshuva, Yoreh Deah, siman 271, se'if katan 13, where I wrote in the name of the new responsa of Radbaz, siman 156, regarding the practice of scribes to fold the paper on which they write the get in place of ruling lines. He writes that if the paper is firm enough that the folds will remain and be recognizable until the end of writing the get, this is sufficient. What difference is there whether he rules with a reed or with anything else that remains and is recognizable? The reason is so that the writing should be straight, and here that is achieved. See there. Now I have seen in Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 44, that he also writes that the custom became widespread in his place to fold the paper instead of ruling lines. The hollow of the fold’s crease must face outward, and the get should be written on the raised side of the fold. See there.

pitchei_teshuva.he: שבא מארץ רחוקה. עיין בתשו' פרח שושן כלל א' ס"ס ב' שהביא דכ"כ בתשו' מהרש"ך ח"ב סי' ה' דכל היכא דהשיירות מצויות לא מקרי שעת הדחק וכ"כ בת' הרד"ך סוף בית ג' מיהו בתשו' הריב"ז סי' ש"מ כתב דהאומר דהיכא שהמקום קרוב והשיירות מצויות אין כאן חשש עיגון כלל קרוב בעיני שזה טעות בדבר משנה דתנן המביא גט ממדינה למדינה במ"ה צ"ל בפ"נ ובפנ"ח כו' ואמרינן עלה ובדין הוא דלובעי תרי אלא משום עיגונא אקילו בה רבנן כו' אלמא דאפי' ממקום קרוב איכא למיחש לעיגונא דלא נתני דבריהם לשיעורין כו' וטעמא דמסתבר הוא דמאן לימא לן שבעוד שחוזר הגט לא ילך הבעל למ"ה או יבטל השליח או ימות ואין שליט ברוח ואין שלטון כו' ע"ש. שוב ראיתי בס' ג"פ ס"ק ע"ט הביא ג"כ דברי הרדב"ז הנ"ל וחולק עליו ומסיק דאין לסמוך ע"ז להקל ולומר דהשתא בכל אתר יש עיגון דבכל דוכתא דשיירות מצויו' לאו מקום עיגון חשיב וכן העלה הרב מהרד"ך כו' ע"ש וגם בסי' קכ"ו ס"ק ס"ה הזכיר קצת מזה ע"ש. ועיין בס' בית מאיר ס"ו כתב דמה שהשיב הג"פ על ראיית הרדב"ז הנ"ל אינו מובן כו' (גם אני בנ"צ כתבתי לתמיה על הג"פ בזה מצד אחר) אך לדינא יפה כיון הג"פ דכן פי' רש"י להדיא דף י"ט בשעת הדחק שהלך זה לדרכו או נישת ומתקנת נאמנות השליח אין ללמוד כלל דמשום עיגון קל האמינוהו ותדע שהרי אף בהבאת גט שחרור נאמן כו' אבל לענינים אחרים צריך שעת הדחק ממש עכ"ד ועמ"ש לעיל סי' מ"ב סק"ו:
pitchei_teshuva.en: That came from a distant land. See the responsum Perach Shoshan, kelal 1, end of siman 2, who cites that the responsa of Maharshach, part 2, siman 5, also writes that wherever caravans are common, it is not called a pressing circumstance. The responsa of the Radach, end of bayit 3, also writes this. However, the responsa of Rivaz, siman 340, writes that one who says that where the place is close and caravans are common there is no concern of igun at all, in his eyes this is close to an error in an explicit Mishnah. For we learned: One who brings a get from one country to another overseas must say, “It was written before me and signed before me.” The Gemara says about this that by right we should require two witnesses, but because of igun the Sages were lenient. This shows that even from a nearby place there is concern of igun, for the Sages did not make their words depend on measures. The reason is logical: who can tell us that while the get is being returned, the husband will not go overseas, or nullify the agency, or die? No one has control over the spirit, and there is no dominion. See there. I later saw in Ginat Veradim, se'if katan 79, that he also cites the above words of the Radbaz, disagrees with him, and concludes that one may not rely on this to be lenient and say that now in every place there is igun. Wherever caravans are common, it is not considered a place of igun. So too concluded Rabbi Maharadach. See there. He also mentions some of this in siman 126, se'if katan 65. See there. See Beit Meir, se'if 6, who writes that what the Ginat Veradim answered against the above proof of the Radbaz is not understandable. I also wrote in Nachalat Tzvi to question the Ginat Veradim on this from another angle. However, as to the law, the Ginat Veradim was correct, for Rashi explicitly explains on page 19 that “pressing circumstances” means that this person went on his way or she remarried. One cannot learn anything from the enactment of believing the agent, because they believed him due to a light concern of igun. Know this, for even when bringing a bill of manumission, he is believed. But for other matters, actual pressing circumstances are required. These are his words. See also what I wrote above, siman 42, se'if katan 6.
